items.title: Evan Christopher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 1, 2009
items.q: this is different than like Benny Goodman or Artie Shaw or any of the Swing Era clarinet players that I loved so much.

ctx.x: And that’s why I don’t use it. I think for me it’s a pejorative term for the music that creates a lot of misunderstanding about the New Orleans tradition. Even friends of mine, colleagues of mine in New York don’t have, they don’t give me evidence they really have any understanding of New Orleans’ music, its significance to them, and they certainly don’t know any of the repertoire. But I think there’s a New York sort of Dixieland tradition that I think they understand better. And the reason I don’t use it is…

actually just came up out of the ground and so the parade had its own soundtrack. But in the interim, before they got ready for the parade they played some music of some musicians that used to be at Disneyland and one of them was a Louisiana clarinetist. He wasn’t New Orleans, in fact it was Baton Rouge, but he worked with Kid Ory. His name was Joe Darensbourg. And he ended up on the west coast. And Joe had a wonderful kind of Creole sound on his clarinet and it was I remember one of the first times I remember…
